_doc: The Actions-minute budget for this repository. Read by
scripts/check_actions_budget.py, which FAILS when the projected month
exceeds `hard_ceiling_minutes` (and WARNS, without failing, when it exceeds
the `design_target_minutes`), when a workflow file has no entry here,
when an entry's crons or job count no longer match the workflow, or when
the projection changes without this file changing.
WHY A CAP AND NOT A HOPE. This repository is private, so every job bills
against the account allowance. On 2026-10-18 the account was refused at
runner-assignment: about 2,016 minutes had been consumed by the 18th,
i.e. about 3,360 in a month, against an allowance of 2,000. The owner
cannot buy more (no USD access from Nepal). The reserve below is the
margin, so this repository must live under the cap, not the allowance.
HOW THE NUMBERS WERE CHOSEN. `p95_minutes` is PER JOB, and it is the
calibration from the measured October consumption, not the workflow
timeout -- a budget built on timeouts flags everything and gets ignored.
`max_runs_per_day` is what the workflow is ALLOWED to produce, not what
GitHub's scheduler actually delivers: GitHub `schedule` is demonstrably
not a clock here (crons aimed at 07:50 and 19:50 Nepal time landed near
12:55 and 23:01), so an hourly cron does not mean 24 runs a day.
MEASURED OCTOBER, per the account audit: daily-news 862 min over 141
runs, drift-canary 393 over 41 (4 jobs each), digest-prebuild 233 over
26 (2 jobs each), breaking-monitor 225 over 140, academic-result 179
over 84, digest-watchdog 124 over 124. 18 days, hence x30/18 for a month.
THIS IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT THE METER. The token cannot read the billing
endpoints (it lacks the `user` scope), so no endpoint can be asked what
was actually spent. budget-sentinel.yml is the runtime half: it measures
real job durations instead of declaring them.
TWO NUMBERS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE, NEVER CONFUSED (2026-10-20).
`design_target_minutes` (1,400) is an ASPIRATION: what this repository
should cost. It is REPORTED, never ENFORCED -- the checker WARNS on it and
budget-sentinel.yml reports it, and neither refuses anything on it. Refusing
at 1,400 would stop work while 600 minutes of allowance were still unspent,
and the owner would lose digests he could have had. `hard_ceiling_minutes`
(1,800) is the number that IS enforced: the included allowance (2,000) minus
`budget_reserve_minutes` (200). budget-sentinel.yml warns at 80% of it,
freezes at 90%, and FAILS at 100%; the Worker's runtime quota reports on it,
and refuses on it ONLY while `enforcement.enabled` is true -- which it is not.
ENFORCEMENT IS A SWITCH, SEPARATE FROM THE ARITHMETIC (2026-10-25).
`enforcement.enabled` says whether the Worker may REFUSE a dispatch once the
month is at the hard ceiling. It is false because this repository is now
PUBLIC, where standard runners are free: a refusal buys no minutes and can
only cost a digest. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED. The numbers above are untouched and
still checked; the static gate still fails a commit that raises the
projection over the ceiling; the sentinel still warns/freezes/fails at
80/90/100%; and the Worker still charges every dispatch to its KV month
record and still reports `budget{}` on `?health=1`. Only the blocking is off.
Set `enabled` back to true to re-arm it -- the repository could go private again.
WHY 200 AND NOT MORE. 200 is the measured model error kept as margin. The
last comparable month came in 282 minutes (9.2%) above its own model (3,360
measured vs 3,078 modelled), and the reserve is ~71% of that: a full 282 would
put the ceiling at 1,718 -- BELOW the current model of 1,746 -- and make the
guard red every single day, which is the behaviour this repository forbids.
The residual 82 minutes of observed risk is absorbed by the freeze arm, which
sheds about 528 minutes of discretionary dispatches when it trips.
1,746 REPLACES THE STALE 3,138 AND IS WHAT THIS TREE ACTUALLY COMPUTES.
3,138 was 3,078 plus the 60 this file's own guard costs (budget-sentinel.yml,
1 run x 1 job x 2.0 x 30). THREE changes took it down, all 2026-10-19/20:
the cron cuts plus the job merges recorded per-workflow below (drift-canary to
ONE job on ONE cron, digest-prebuild to ONE job with no schedule, academic-result
24 -> 2 firings, breaking-monitor 4 -> 1); narrowing the prebuild poll from
20x15s to 5x6s (prebuild p95 4.5 -> 1.5, 270 -> 90 a month); and moving the
empty-digest retry ladder off digest-watchdog.yml's 72-a-day GitHub cron onto
the Worker's own minute grid (watchdog 7 -> 2 runs a day, 210 -> 60).
1,746 SITS ABOVE THE DESIGN TARGET (1,400) AND BELOW THE HARD CEILING
(1,800), SO THE CHECKER WARNS AND PASSES. The design-target overage is a
REPORT, not a failure; the enforced number is not breached. The single
remaining lever is still daily-news.yml (1,098 of the 1,746: a 6.1-minute
agent run at 6 runs a day, 2.4x the architect's 570 target), and cutting it
means fewer builds of the digest itself -- see the note beside that entry.
Every other line is already at or under its target.

enforcement.reason: public repository - standard runners are free
enforcement._re_enable: Flip `enabled` to true to put the hard-ceiling refusal back, and flip BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED in deploy/cloudflare-worker.js with it -- the Worker cannot read this file at runtime, so Check 21 fails if the two disagree.
enforcement._visibility_probe: The Worker asks GitHub for `.private` at most once every 6 hours (KV key `budget:visibility`) and force-disables enforcement while the answer is public, whatever `enabled` says. A probe that cannot answer (no token, non-200, no boolean `private`) is NOT read as public: `enabled` decides, which is why the switch must still work on its own.

_cuts_2026_10_19: drift-canary.yml: the 'Dispatch daily digest dry-run and wait' step was
removed (2 dispatches a day of the real digest, ~366 min/month at the
calibrated 6.1 min/run); the job also no longer holds `actions: write`,
because nothing in it dispatches any more.
firings a day, 5 -> 2 runs a day, ~189 min/month).
a day, 8 -> 5 runs a day, ~144 min/month), the Worker remaining primary.
Total cut: 3,777 -> 3,078 minutes a month (699 saved).

budget-sentinel.yml.why: The guard's own cost, budgeted like everything else -- a detector that is not in the budget is the first thing to make the budget a lie. One job a day; 2 minutes rather than 1 because it makes one API call per run in its window (~200), and the step prints its own elapsed time.

daily-news.yml.why: The most expensive single thing here: one job, but a real agent run. Two schedule firings plus the Worker's dispatches. 8 -> 6 runs a day on 2026-10-19, when Drift Canary's two daily dry-run dispatches were removed. AT 1,098 MINUTES THIS IS 53% OF THE WHOLE BUDGET AND 2.4x THE ARCHITECT'S 570 TARGET, and it is the ONLY line that can close the remaining 676-minute gap: 570 implies ~3.1 runs a day at the measured 6.1 minutes, i.e. HALF the current volume. That is not a cron to trim -- it is the digest build, its prebuild dispatch and its fallback/re-fire ceiling, so cutting it trades a delivery guarantee for minutes. Left at 6 deliberately; recorded here so the trade is visible rather than made quietly.

drift-canary.yml.why: ONE job per run since 2026-10-19 (B): docs-lint, drift-canary, the live-parser canary and the stdlib suite now share one job on one daily cron, so a run costs 1 billed minute minimum instead of 4, and a single `timeout-minutes: 25` replaces the four separate budgets (5+60+12+10). The '17 3 * * *' cron went in the same change, so 3 runs a day became 1.

digest-prebuild.yml.why: No schedule: dispatched by the Worker, so it is absent from any cron arithmetic and still a real cost. ONE job per run since 2026-10-19 (A): the `dispatch` job that dialled daily-news.yml and then waited up to 45 minutes for it is gone, and the build now hands the seal its OWN run id as its last step, so nothing watches anything. `p95_minutes` was carried over from the two-job measurement at 4.5 while the seal still polled; NARROWED TO 1.5 on 2026-10-20 once the poll went from 20x15s to 5x6s. The hand-off step that dials the seal is gated `success()` and is the build job's LAST step, so the run has already concluded by the time the seal starts and only GitHub's read eventual-consistency remained. The 1.5 is checkout + the artifact reads + the record/supersede work, and it is STILL AN ESTIMATE: no run has been timed since the job merge, so budget-sentinel.yml confirms or refutes it.

breaking-monitor.yml.why: The Worker dispatches it on its own schedule and is the sensor; the cron is the late-tolerant backstop and was cut from 4 firings a day to 1 on 2026-10-19 (8 -> 5 runs a day). A dead Worker is now noticed within ~24 hours rather than 6.

academic-result.yml.why: Worker-dispatched on detection; the cron is the dead-man's backstop and was cut from 24 firings a day to 2 on 2026-10-19 (09:02 and 15:02 Nepal time, inside TU office hours). KNOWN LIMIT: the measured 4.7 runs a day was the congested hourly backstop plus rare result dispatches, and the split cannot be recovered from the aggregate -- so this entry declares the 2 scheduled firings and lets budget-sentinel.yml see any dispatch-driven spike rather than assuming one here.

digest-watchdog.yml.why: TWO runs a day since 2026-10-20, down from seven. The 17,32,47 empty-digest retry ladder was removed from this workflow's `schedule:` and moved onto the Worker's own minute grid (SCHED_LADDER_PHASE in deploy/cloudflare-worker.js), which dials this workflow with ladder_only=true only when state/digest_retry.json says a retry is due -- at most twice a day, and those land inside the same pair. Billed at ONE job per run throughout: `watchdog` is gated to the 04/16 firing and never rides the ladder. The 124 minutes measured in October were the ladder's 72 daily minute-long checks plus the pair; that is the cost this change removes.
